To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) higher levels of physical inactivity increase risk of developing certain types of cancer; (2) physical activity can reduce cancer treatment-related symptoms; and (3) physical activity is safe for cancer survivors.
physical activity is associated with a reduced risk of cancer incidence and mortality, and physical activity during and after cancer therapy improves physical and psychosocial health.
there are a large number of epidemiologic and clinical studies that have examined the relationship between physical inactivity and cancer risk and cancer treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between physical exercise and the risk of cancer and its treatment.
the effects of physical activity on cancer incidence and survival, and with the effects of exercise training on the quality of life of cancer survivors.
the role of physical activity across the cancer continuum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
physical activity is a safe and efficacious adjunct for the prevention of cancer, as well as for the treatment of cancer.
physical activity is associated with a reduction in cancer incidence and recurrence, and that physical activity is a safe and effective adjunctive therapy to reduce cancer treatment-related symptoms.
physical activity and exercise can be beneficial to the cancer survivor, both during and after cancer therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
physical activity is a promising tool to reduce the risk of developing certain cancers and to alleviate many symptoms of cancer and its treatment.
physical activity is a promising intervention that can improve the lives of cancer patients and survivors.
there is sufficient evidence to recommend physical activity for the prevention and treatment of cancer, and that the benefits are similar to those seen in healthy adults.
The main takeaway from our work is that
physical activity is a safe and effective adjunct to cancer treatment, and should be considered as a part of standard of care for all survivors.
the evidence base is strong enough to recommend physical activity as an adjunct to standard treatment for cancer survivors.
there is a strong and consistent body of research that demonstrates the benefits of physical activity across the cancer continuum.
